120290101.text: Alright, Miko, we're here. So, what's your plan of action to deal with this rival book?

120290102.text: Hmm... Why don't you take a guess?

120290103.text: I'll give you a hint. It's to do with the Yae Publishing House.

120290104.text: Hmmmm... Oh, Paimon knows! Combine the reputation of the Yae Publishing House with the status of Guuji Yae and tell everyone that the incantations in that book are dangerous!

120290105.text: Ooh, wow! Your first guess, and you got it absolutely...

120290107.text: Yeah— Aww! ...Wait, seriously? That wasn't it?

120290108.text: "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" is the hottest light novel right now. If we did as you suggested, we would effectively be advertising to everyone that the incantations are real.

120290109.text: In bending over backwards trying to warn everyone about the dangers, all we would accomplish is to create more curious readers ready to try them out. Also, sales for the book would only increase further.

120290110.text: Okay, yeah, that would be pretty catastrophic... Oh! How about we confiscate all the copies?

120290111.text: *sigh* Leaving aside the issue of the enormous manpower and resources such an operation would require, going to such lengths over a light novel would be extremely disruptive to the lives of Inazumans.

120290112.text: But that means there's nothing we can do...

120290114.text: I've read "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits." It has many other good qualities besides the incantations alone.

120290115.text: The book contains many ancient "kaidan" — or tales of the supernatural — and is written in a very engaging way. That is why the book has become so popular.

120290116.text: I think we're going to have a difficult time trying to rein in its popularity while it's the only work in its league on the market.

120290118.text: That's right. How do you get rid of the next big thing? You replace it with the next next big thing.

120290119.text: So what we're going to do is create Inazuma's newest hit novel.

120290120.text: Smash our rival's sales numbers and win our readers back. That is how Yae Miko wages war!

120290121.text: Incidentally, this will also be the best way to combat the influence of "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits."

120290122.text: Wait, Miko, so you want us to write a novel?

120290125.text: Heh, well, becoming an accomplished novelist certainly isn't an overnight process. But let's not forget that I am the chief editor of the Yae Publishing House. I have my ways.

120290126.text: I did say this is what "we're" going to do. I trust that the word "teamwork" is in your vocabulary.

120290127.text: Anyway. There's a writers' submission event going on at the moment. Start by talking to readers and finding out what they're into. When you have an idea of what the current trends are, come back and see me.

120290128.text: I'll be at Uyuu Restaurant — find me there when you're done. I will assemble a team, and we can work while we eat.

120290301.text: The Yae Publishing House has held many writers' submission events to date.

120290302.text: The winner gets a huge amount of publicity. It's been the ticket to fame for a lot of authors! If you've got a good idea for a story, you definitely don't want to miss out!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the submission event to listen to what the readers like

120290901.text: I've been reading light novels for long time now. I'm mainly into big, ambitious fantasy works with an original core concept and good storytelling.

120290902.text: These days, though, everyone seems to be imitating each other. Most of the time I can guess what the story is about just from the title.

120290903.text: The only recent book worth mentioning is "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits."

120290904.text: Not only is it a good story, but the descriptions are really true to life. So much so that I'm almost wondering if maybe the author really has met all those youkai before.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the submission event to listen to what the readers like

120290601.text: The key to a successful light novel is having good illustrations.

120290602.text: When to use illustrations, what they should contain, and which artist you should commission for them... These are all key things to bear in mind.

120290603.text: Good illustrations can make up for bad writing. But on the flip side, a bad illustration can ruin your novel, even if you have the best story in the world.

120290604.text: There's a saying that light novels are essentially a case of "buy art, get words free." I'd agree with that. Too bad most of the top artists have jam-packed schedules, so it's extremely difficult to commission them...

120290605.text: The illustrations in "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" are incredible, but it's unlike any art style I've ever seen before.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the submission event to listen to what the readers like

120290701.text: I'll be honest. I read light novels for the cheap thrills.

120290702.text: In most traditional stories, the protagonist usually has this long and drawn out character arc, usually involving a process of separation, loss, and ultimately growth and renewed strength. It reads well, and everything, it's just a little slow-paced for me.

120290703.text: By contrast, there's this popular light novel at the moment called "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits," where the protagonist is super strong right from the get-go! That's what I mean by cheap thrills: action-packed right from page one.

120290704.text: The protagonist is a kitsune who has not only mastered the secret art of incantations, but also tea ceremony, painting, and calligraphy!

120290201.text: How did it go? What did you learn?

120290202.text: We learned a couple of things...

120290203.text: You tell Yae Miko the readers' thoughts.

120290204.text: All very true. An original core concept, a fast pace, quality illustrations, and lots of action. This is the formula that will guarantee good sales numbers.

120290205.text: It's getting late. Let's go to Uyuu Restaurant and write as we eat.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to Uyuu Restaurant to finish the light novel

120291301.text: Ah, there you are. Let me introduce the team:

120291302.text: You've already met Junkichi and Shigeru.

120291303.text: Shigeru is an experienced editor and Junkichi is the author he's partnered with. Junkichi's working through a creative lull at the moment, but all his past works have been very popular with young people. He has developed a distinct and enduringly popular style.

120291304.text: Satomi is Yae Publishing House's ace in the hole. Her specialty is that she can write all kinds of completely different stories, and all under different pen names. As for what those names are, well, that's a trade secret.

120291305.text: They will be teaming up with us to collectively create the novel that knocks "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" off its perch. So? Feeling better about my plan now?

120291306.text: Uh-huh, it definitely makes sense! Hehe.

120291307.text: Now then, tell me what you found out about readers' preferences.

120291308.text: You tell Yae Miko the readers' thoughts.

120291309.text: All very true. An original core concept, a fast pace, quality illustrations, and lots of action. This is the formula that will guarantee good sales numbers.

120291310.text: More importantly than that, even though it's a work of fiction, we have to deliver a sense of realism.

120291311.text: Paimon followed pretty much all of that, but there's still one question... what are we actually gonna write about?

120291312.text: For example, we know we need an original core concept... but how do we come up with one?

120291313.text: Hehe... Before you can answer that question, you have to understand your target audience.

120291314.text: Take "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits," for example. When I read it, all I find is common knowledge to the kitsune. But to the general public, it's bursting with new and interesting ideas. It all comes down to the size of the information gap between author and reader.

120291315.text: As a Traveler, there must be a great many things you know about that are complete unknowns to the people of Inazuma. What is commonplace to you may be fresh and original to them.

120291316.text: Ohh, right! So maybe we can take inspiration from our time in Mondstadt and Liyue!

120291317.text: Hmm, but that would make it a completely different genre than "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits"... Uh, is that gonna be a problem?

120291318.text: Not at all. You don't have to worry so much about how to compete with that book. All you have to do is provide some interesting ideas based on your travel experiences.

120291319.text: As long as the core content is interesting, my expert team here will be able to flesh out the details.

120291320.text: #Alright! Let's start with chapter one, then. Uh... what are you thinking, {NICKNAME}?

120291322.text: No! No one would ever go for that, no matter how you tried to play it!

120291323.text: Hmm... Out of a maximum of 10 points, I'd give that a 9!

120291324.text: Is there really flying emergency food in other worlds? How does it taste? And how do you cook it?

120291325.text: It's a strong opening — an easy way to grab the readers' attention. Never underestimate the appeal of culinary-oriented subject matter. Food, after all, is a topic that everyone is interested in.

120291346.text: Good job, little one. You're not only drawing on your own experiences, but it seems you're filtering them through the lens of the kinds of light novels you've read in the past. I think you really understand what we're trying to do here.

120291347.text: Thoughts from the experts? Are we able to work with this general framework to make an interesting story?

120291348.text: Yeah, we think it works. I tend to overcomplicate the core concept if I'm not careful, so this deals with that problem.

120291350.text: Okay, we're done with chapter one. Let's move on to chapter two.

120291351.text: Huh? Won't that do for now?

120291352.text: Readers will devour your content a lot more quickly than you'd think. If we don't keep delivering the goods now we've caught their attention, all our hard work so far is in vain.

120291353.text: Hurry, chapter two, let's go. Can't you see that Satomi is waiting?

120291354.text: #Hmm? What's wrong with you, {NICKNAME}? You don't look so good...

120291328.text: Let's see what you've got... "After enrolling in the Mondstadt Academy, I found out that the young man sitting next to me in class was a total slacker."

120291329.text: "He said he was a bard, had a habit of playing his lyre in class, and always had a bottle of liquor on his person. But his true identity was actually the principal of the academy..."

120291330.text: What kind of plot is that!?

120291331.text: Hmm... Out of a maximum of 10 points, I'd give that a 9.5!

120291332.text: It just goes to show, you have to have an interesting character sitting in the back row by the window.

120291333.text: The protagonist is a transfer student, new to the school, whose ordinary life is about to take a wild turn when they meet the ballad-and-alcohol-loving principal. Sounds interesting. Approved!

120291334.text: Paimon just does not see the appeal...

120291336.text: This sounds like a great one!

120291337.text: Let's see here... "The protagonist arrives in Mondstadt for the first time to the sight of a dragon flying around and wreaking havoc on the city."

120291338.text: "With the help of some trusty companions, the protagonist successfully defeats the dragon. But then... the dragon suddenly turns into a beautiful young woman..." ...Huh?

120291339.text: "Human, let us work together to build a better future! The love story between human and dragon begins today..."

120291340.text: Well that was an unexpected development. What happened to the grand adventure!?

120291341.text: "The Grand Adventure" is just the protagonist's name.

120291343.text: Hmm... Out of a maximum of 10 points, I'd give that a 9!

120291344.text: The story certainly goes in an unorthodox direction. And the dragon-girl sounds destined to be a hit character. Approved!

120291501.text: After "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" took off, a whole host of copycat works appeared on the market. But they were such low quality that no one paid them any attention.

120291502.text: It just goes to show that you should write to your own interests. If you just try and imitate someone else, you'll lose your way.

120291201.text: I've finished "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" now. I wonder if I'll ever be able to find another one as good as that?

120291202.text: If I can't find anything else to my liking, I guess I'll just have to read "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" again.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to Yae Publishing House to complete the endorsement

120290401.text: You tell Kuroda about the situation...

120290402.text: Ms. Hina doesn't usually do endorsements. But since it's Lady Guuji that's asking, we'll see what we can do.

120290403.text: With Ms. Hina getting so popular lately, a lot of people have come to us hoping to do a collaboration.

120290404.text: But Ms. Hina's not interested in any of it. She still prefers to focus all her efforts on replying to readers' letters, and turns down every promotional opportunity she can.

120290405.text: Maybe that's why her fans like her so much... Ahem, I'm getting off topic here. Anyway, if we can get that endorsement from Ms. Hina, you'll definitely get an exposure boost at the beginning.

120290406.text: May your light novel sell well, and set a new record for the Yae Publishing House!

120290801.text: Yae Miko brings the completed light novel...

120290802.text: Are you sure you'd like to submit this entry? Let me see, "The Miraculous Adventures of the Traveler," by "Thousand Hands."

120290803.text: What a strange pen name... Definitely your doing. Having been around you so much recently, Paimon's slowly starting to understand your unique tastes.

120290804.text: What do you mean, "strange"? It took a lot of work by a lot of different people to get this thing finished. Don't you think it's a very descriptive pen name?

120290805.text: We'll get this printed as a matter of priority and conduct trial sales in pilot locations throughout Inazuma. I'll announce the sales numbers in three days.

120290806.text: #Uh-oh, Paimon's getting a little nervous now. D'you really think this is gonna work, {NICKNAME}?

120290809.text: That's right, be confident in your work. That's exactly how a light novelist should be.

120290810.text: Okay, then I'll sign you up. Please come back in three days for the results.

120290811.text: Thank you all for your submission. I wish you the very best of luck!

120290501.text: Ah, you've all finally made it.

120290502.text: Good news, everyone. I just received word that your light novel is flying off the shelves! Multiple sales locations are asking when we'll be printing more copies.

120290504.text: This level of success is an amazing accomplishment for a new work. Most new books don't sell 30% of what you've sold.

120290505.text: I have free copies for each of you here, please take them. The payment will follow shortly, and I'll notify you to come and collect it when the time comes.

120290507.text: Oh, yeah! The whole reason why we made this light novel was to combat the influence of "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits."

120290508.text: Hmm, we sold a lot of copies, but it doesn't feel like we accomplished our goal. How do we know whether it worked?

120290509.text: Hehe... Oh, don't worry. The change is already underway.

120290510.text: Shh... listen to what the people around us are talking about. The conversation has already moved on, hasn't it?

120290511.text: Hey guys... have you heard about this latest kaidan thing doing the rounds? You just need to recite the incantation from "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" at midnight, and your wish will come true...

120290512.text: Oh, that? Heh, that's a throwback. That's old news, man.

120290513.text: No one's talking about that anymore. "The Secret Spells of Lady Kitsune" is the new hit thing. I've already memorized all the incantations.

120290514.text: "The Secret Spells of Lady Kitsune"? What's that?

120290515.text: You haven't read it yet? Okay, so, supposedly, if you recite the spell in there on a moonless night, you'll receive the protection of the kitsune and all the other powerful youkai. They can make any of your wishes come true!

120290516.text: I heard that the incantations in "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" have weird side effects! This one guy wished for a load of Mora — and got it — but then one night, it all turned to leaves and he developed a high fever.

120290517.text: They actually had to use one of "The Secret Spells of Lady Kitsune" to get rid of the discomfort.

120290518.text: That proves that the incantations in this book are more potent than the ones everyone was trying before! Pretty much everyone I know is desperate to try it out — just waiting for a moonless night.

120290519.text: Really? Well I'd better go and prepare, too...

120290521.text: Wow, you're right. Everyone's shifting focus!

120290522.text: But what's this "moonless night" that they're talking about?

120290523.text: Paimon doesn't remember that detail from the brainstorming session.

120290524.text: Hehe, this is something that will become very important to us further down the line. Alright, it's time to move on to the next phase of the plan.

120290526.text: Of course. Behind every book that hits the market lies an author, right?

120290527.text: Ohh, yeah! If we leave him to his own devices, he might just write another guide to summoning spirits.

120290528.text: ...Also, we still need to figure out what his motive for writing it was!

120290529.text: Exactly, that's what we need to take care of next. Fortunately, I've already managed to identify the author — he's a failed light novelist named Tomoyuki.

120290530.text: But when we went to ask him about it, he had no recollection whatsoever of having written the book.

120290532.text: Yes, this is another case of possession — only this time, whoever possessed him actively sought him out.

120290533.text: After his novel submission failed, he was walking aimlessly in Araumi. In frustration, he shouted out: "Please, someone, anyone! Help me write a truly amazing novel!" After that, he lost consciousness.

120290534.text: But the spirit that wrote the book has already left him now, right? So what are we supposed to do?

120290535.text: Simple. It wrote a summoning incantation in the book, didn't it? So we can just use its own method to make it manifest itself.

120290536.text: And you, my little friend, are the perfect candidate for this role. Hehehe...

120290539.text: Aww, what are you talking about? The fun's just about to begin.

120291423.text: Let me think... What spell does Lady Kitsune teach to the protagonist? ...Ah, I've got it!

120291424.text: Hee-hee, I've got to make sure it sounds suitably mysterious...

120291601.text: I don't usually like the kaidan genre, but "The Secret Spells of Lady Kitsune" is an exception.

120291602.text: I'm definitely going to give it a try as soon as we have a moonless night. Here's hoping Lady Kitsune will make my wishes come true...

120291701.text: I bought three copies of this light novel. One to read, one for my collection, and another one to lend out to my friends.

120291702.text: It's worth the price just for the gorgeous illustrations alone!

120291801.text: Honestly, it's a really gripping story. I'm still feeling pumped up!

120291802.text: I hope the next volume comes out soon... Wait, when is it coming out, actually? Aw man, I hope it won't be a really long wait...

120291901.text: Wow... I never expected this submission event would uncover such talented authors.

120291902.text: To make sure you can all deliver your best work, we should fix an issue date for the next volume now.

120292801.text: Don't worry, this story has a very clear narrative structure. Junkichi will definitely be able to work his magic on the writing front.

120292802.text: Oh yeah, how did it go with that incantation from "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits"? Did you manage to make a wish in the end?

120292803.text: Nope! On the first day, Junkichi couldn't memorize the incantation, because it was too long. On the second day, he didn't wake up in time, and midnight came and went. Then, on the third day—

120292804.text: Mr. Shigeru, I thought we agreed not to speak of this?

120292901.text: Hmm... add a little foreshadowing here... callback to the first chapter there — callback via contrast, that is... plot twist here, obviously. Now, where's the best to explore the central theme...

120292902.text: Wow, she seems really in the zone. Let's not disturb her.

120293001.text: Have you made a submission? Wow, you turned that around pretty quickly! Seems like I'm in for a treat soon, haha!

120293101.text: I'm not buying it unless the illustrations are good.

120293201.text: I've finished "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" now. I wonder if I'll be able to find another one as good as that?

120293202.text: If I can't find anything else to my liking, I guess I'll just have to read "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits" again.

120293301.text: Lady Guuji has an eye for things like this. If she thinks your work is interesting, you can be sure it's destined for success.

120293401.text: Yae Publishing House's submission event is in full swing!

120293402.text: Unleash your talent! Become the one light novelist to rule them all!

120293502.text: Thank you all for your participation! The sales rankings for this round of submissions are as follows—

120293503.text: 1st Place: "The Miraculous Adventures of the Traveler"
